text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will chair a meeting of the Socialists' national board today to discuss preparations for the party's June congress and the latest developments in the Operation Birch Tree case, where data on several MPs were illegally gathered by civil intelligence staff.

- The cabinet is expected today to discuss details of pension reform and the fate of the current potato surplus. The cabinet is also set to examine the privatisation of Mezobank, as well as discussing the current position of Postabank.
- NATO's military committee in Brussels discussed Wednesday principles and frameworks for a future Euro-Atlantic partnership council, set to replace the current Partnership for Peace programme.

- Though growth in the Hungarian economy has slowed down, the government's financial policy has created the foundations for sustainable expansion; inflation is likely to go down from last year's 24 percent to 18 percent, concludes an IMF report.
- Dunaholding Rt. closed the sixth year of its operation with 871 milion forints pre-tax profits.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The costs of Hungary's joining NATO are put at an annual 8 to 9 billion forints, according to the Hungarian Atlantic Council.
- The health and pension insurance sectors had together accumulated nearly 20 billion forints in deficit as of late March, according to initial figures.
- An Irish bank and a Belgian consortium will compete to purchase a stake of at least 25 percent in K&H Bank.
- Some $2 million support from the EU's PHARE programme will be directed toward upgrading the security systems of several East European power plants, including the nuclear power station at Paks.
- Every tenth CD bought in Hungary is a pirate copy, according to the Association of Hungarian Record Companies. Insiders know that most of the bootlegged discs come from Bulgaria.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Istvan Csurka, president of the far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP), heavily criticised the European Union of Christian Democrats for threatening Hungary's Christian Democrats with expulsion should they form an alliance with MIEP.
- For the first time in Hungary, a lawsuit has been filed and won against the construction of a shopping mall being built by the French company Auchan near Budaors.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs signed an agreement in Hanoi on Wednesday on maintaining regular contacts between the Hungarian and Vietnamese Foreign Ministries. NAPI GAZDASAG
- The performance of the construction industry is likely to increase by four to five percent this year.
- Hungary's largest gas company Tigaz Rt. generated one billion forints after-tax profits on net revenues of 45.8 billion forints last year.

- The annual general meeting of Horizon-Multiplan brought violent arguments between management and shareholders yesterday. Owners resigned themselves to last year's 96 million forints loss, a far cry from the profits projected early in 1996.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
